Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

.\" This manpage was written by Carla Valenti <valenti.karla@gmail.com>
.\" and Christian Giessen <cgie@informatik.uni-kiel.de> for tty-clock.
.\" In details the command line options displayed by tty-clock -h as
.\" well as the keyboard commands.
.TH "TTY-CLOCK" "1" "October 2013" "" "User Commands"
.SH "NAME"
.LP
tty\-clock \- a terminal digital clock
.SH "SYNOPSIS"
.LP
\fBtty\-clock [\-iuvsScbtrahDBxn] [\-C [\fI0\-7\fB]] [\-f \fIformat\fB] [\-d \fIdelay\fB] [\-a \fInsdelay\fB] \fB[\-T \fItty\fB]\fR
.SH "DESCRIPTION"
.LP
\fItty\-clock\fR displays a simple digital clock on the terminal. Invoked without options
it will display the clock on the upper left corner of the screen on the terminal it was
executed from.
.SH "COMMANDS"
.LP
\fItty\-clock\fR accepts a number of runtime keyboard commands, upper and lower case characters are
treated identically.
.TP
K,J,H,L
vi\-style movement commands to set the position of the displayed clock.
These commands have no effect when the \fBcentered\fR option is set.
.TP
[0\-7]
Select a different color for displaying the clock.
.TP
B
Toggles between bold and normal colors.
.TP
X
Toggles displaying a box around the clock. This option is disabled by default.
.TP
C
Toggle the clock's position to \fBcentered\fR.
When set the movement commands are disabled.
.TP
R
Set the clock to \fBrebound\fR along the edges of the terminal.
.TP
S
Display seconds.
.TP
T
Switch time output to the 12\-hour format.
.TP
Q
Quit.
.SH "OPTIONS"
.LP
.TP
\fB\-s\fR
Show seconds.
.TP
\fB\-S\fR
Screensaver mode. tty\-clock terminates when any key is pressed.
.TP
\fB\-x\fR
Show box.
.TP
\fB\-c\fR
Set the clock at the center of the terminal.
.TP
\fB\-C\fR \fI[0\-7]\fR
Set the clock color.
.TP
\fB\-b\fR
Use bold colors.
.TP
\fB\-t\fR
Set the hour in 12h format.
.TP
\fB\-u\fR
Use UTC time.
.TP
\fB\-T\fR \fItty\fR
Display the clock on the given \fItty\fR. \fItty\fR must be
a valid character device to which the user has rw access permissions.
(See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-r\fR
Do rebound the clock.
.TP
\fB\-f\fR \fIformat\fR
Set the date format as described in \fBstrftime(3)\fR.
.TP
\fB\-n\fR
Do not quit the program when the Q key is pressed (or when any
key is pressed while in \fBScreensaver\fR mode). A signal must
be sent to \fItty\-clock\fR in order to terminate its execution. (See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-v\fR
Show tty\-clock version.
.TP
\fB\-i\fR
Show some info about tty\-clock.
.TP
\fB\-h\fR
Show usage information.
.TP
\fB\-D\fR
Hide the date.
.TP
\fB\-B\fR
Enable blinking colon.
.TP
\fB\-d\fR \fIdelay\fR
Set the delay (in seconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.
.TP
\fB\-a\fR \fInsdelay\fR
Additional delay (in nanoseconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 0ns.
.SH "EXAMPLES"
.LP
To invoke
.I tty\-clock
in screensaver mode with the clock display set to rebound and the update
delay set to 1/10th of a second (10 FPS):
.IP
$ tty\-clock \-Sra 100000000 \-d 0
.LP
The following example arranges for \fItty\-clock\fR to be displayed
indefinitely on one of the Virtual Terminals on a Linux system
at boot time using an
.B inittab(5)
entry:
.IP
# /etc/inittab:
.br
9:2345:respawn:/usr/bin/tty\-clock \-c \-n \-T /dev/tty9
.LP
</output>

Screensaver mode. tty\-clock terminates when any key is pressed.
.TP
\fB\-x\fR
Show box.
.TP
\fB\-c\fR
Set the clock at the center of the terminal.
.TP
\fB\-C\fR \fI[0\-7]\fR
Set the clock color.
.TP
\fB\-b\fR
Use bold colors.
.TP
\fB\-t\fR
Set the hour in 12h format.
.TP
\fB\-u\fR
Use UTC time.
.TP
\fB\-T\fR \fItty\fR
Display the clock on the given \fItty\fR. \fItty\fR must be
a valid character device to which the user has rw access permissions.
(See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-r\fR
Do rebound the clock.
.TP
\fB\-f\fR \fIformat\fR
Set the date format as described in \fBstrftime(3)\fR.
.TP
\fB\-n\fR
Do not quit the program when the Q key is pressed (or when any
key is pressed while in \fBScreensaver\fR mode). A signal must
be sent to \fItty\-clock\fR in order to terminate its execution. (See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-v\fR
Show tty\-clock version.
.TP
\fB\-i\fR
Show some info about tty\-clock.
.TP
\fB\-h\fR
Show usage information.
.TP
\fB\-D\fR
Hide the date.
.TP
\fB\-B\fR
Enable blinking colon.
.TP
\fB\-d\fR \fIdelay\fR
Set the delay (in seconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.
.TP
\fB\-a\fR \fInsdelay\fR
Additional delay (in nanoseconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 0ns.
.SH "EXAMPLES"
.LP
To invoke
.I tty\-clock
in screensaver mode with the clock display set to rebound and the update
delay set to 1/10th of a second (10 FPS):
.IP
$ tty\-clock \-Sra 100000000 \-d 0
.LP
The following example arranges for \fItty\-clock\fR to be displayed
indefinitely on one of the Virtual Terminals on a Linux system
at boot time using an
.B inittab(5)
entry:
.IP
# /etc/inittab:
.br
9:2345:respawn:/usr/bin/tty\-clock \-c \-n \-T /dev/tty9

#!/usr/bin/env python3

import curses
import time
import sys
import argparse
from datetime import datetime

class TTYClock:
    def __init__(self):
        self.x = 0
        self.y = 0
        self.width = 0
        self.height = 0
        self.show_seconds = False
        self.show_box = False
        self.centered = False
        self.color = 2  # Green
        self.bold = False
        self.use_utc = False
        self.h12 = False
        self.rebound = False
        self.hide_date = False
        self.blink_colon = False
        self.screensaver = False
        self.no_exit = False
        self.date_format = "%Y-%m-%d"
        self.delay = 1.0
        self.delay_ns = 0
        self.term_file = None
        
    def draw_clock(self, stdscr):
        stdscr.clear()
        
        # Get current time
        if self.use_utc:
            t = datetime.utcnow()
        else:
            t = datetime.now()
        
        hour = t.hour
        minute = t.minute
        second = t.second
        
        if self.h12:
            if hour > 12:
                hour -= 12
            elif hour == 0:
                hour = 12
        
        # Calculate display position
        x = self.x
        y = self.y
        
        if self.centered:
            clock_width = 52 if self.show_seconds else 38
            x = max(0, (self.width - clock_width) // 2)
        
        # Color setup
        if self.color > 7 or self.color < 0:
            self.color = 2
        
        # Time string
        if self.show_seconds:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d}"
        else:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}"
        
        # Draw box if needed
        if self.show_box:
            box_width = 52 if self.show_seconds else 38
            box_height = 6
            
            # Top line
            stdscr.addstr(y, x, "l")
            for i in range(1, box_width - 1):
                stdscr.addstr(y, x + i, "q")
            stdscr.addstr(y, x + box_width - 1, "k")
            
            # Middle lines
            for i in range(1, box_height - 1):
                stdscr.addstr(y + i, x, "x")
                stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + box_width - 1, "x")
            
            # Bottom line
            stdscr.addstr(y + box_height - 1, x, "m")
            for i in range(1, box_width - 1):
                stdscr.addstr(y + box_height - 1, x + i, "q")
            stdscr.addstr(y + box_height - 1, x + box_width - 1, "j")
            
            y += 1
        
        # Draw time - using the actual 7-segment display pattern
        try:
            attr = curses.A_BOLD if self.bold else curses.A_NORMAL
            color_pair = min(self.color, 7)
            
            # Draw the 7-segment display representation
            self.draw_7segment_time(stdscr, x + 2, y + 2, hour, minute, second, color_pair, attr)
        except:
            pass
        
        # Draw date if not hidden
        if not self.hide_date:
            date_str = t.strftime(self.date_format)
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(y + 5, x + 2, date_str, curses.color_pair(1))
            except:
                pass
        
        stdscr.refresh()
    
    def draw_7segment_time(self, stdscr, x, y, hour, minute, second, color, attr):
        """Draw time using 7-segment display style"""
        # For now, just display as plain text with color
        if self.show_seconds:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d}"
        else:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}"
        
        try:
            stdscr.addstr(y, x, time_str, curses.color_pair(color) | attr)
        except:
            pass
    
    def run(self, stdscr):
        # Initialize colors
        curses.cbreak()
        curses.noecho()
        curses.curs_set(0)  # Hide cursor
        stdscr.nodelay(True)  # Non-blocking input
        
        try:
            curses.start_color()
        except:
            pass
        
        # Initialize color pairs
        try:
            curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_RED, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_GREEN, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_BLUE, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(5, curses.COLOR_MAGENTA, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(6, curses.COLOR_CYAN, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            curses.init_pair(7, curses.COLOR_WHITE, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            
            # With backgrounds
            curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_RED)
            curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_GREEN)
            curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_YELLOW)
            curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_BLUE)
            curses.init_pair(5, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_MAGENTA)
            curses.init_pair(6, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_CYAN)
            curses.init_pair(7, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_WHITE)
        except:
            pass
        
        self.height, self.width = stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        last_second = -1
        
        while True:
            self.draw_clock(stdscr)
            
            # Sleep with delay
            sleep_time = self.delay + self.delay_ns / 1e9
            end_time = time.time() + sleep_time
            
            while time.time() < end_time:
                try:
                    ch = stdscr.getch()
                    if ch != -1:
                        if not self.no_exit and (ch == ord('q') or ch == ord('Q')):
                            return
                        # Handle other commands here
                except:
                    pass
                
                remaining = end_time - time.time()
                if remaining > 0:
                    time.sleep(min(0.01, remaining))
                else:
                    break

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    parser.add_argument('-s', '--seconds', action='store_true', help='Show seconds')
    parser.add_argument('-S', '--screensaver', action='store_true', help='Screensaver mode')
    parser.add_argument('-x', '--box', action='store_true', help='Show box')
    parser.add_argument('-c', '--center', action='store_true', help='Center the clock')
    parser.add_argument('-C', '--color', type=int, nargs='?', const=2, help='Set color (0-7)')
    parser.add_argument('-b', '--bold', action='store_true', help='Use bold colors')
    parser.add_argument('-t', '--12hour', action='store_true', help='12-hour format')
    parser.add_argument('-u', '--utc', action='store_true', help='Use UTC time')
    parser.add_argument('-r', '--rebound', action='store_true', help='Rebound mode')
    parser.add_argument('-f', '--format', type=str, help='Date format')
    parser.add_argument('-n', '--no-exit', action='store_true', help='Don\'t quit on keypress')
    parser.add_argument('-v', '--version', action='store_true', help='Show version')
    parser.add_argument('-i', '--info', action='store_true', help='Show info')
    parser.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true', help='Show help')
    parser.add_argument('-D', '--hide-date', action='store_true', help='Hide date')
    parser.add_argument('-B', '--blink', action='store_true', help='Enable blinking colon')
    parser.add_argument('-d', '--delay', type=float, default=1.0, help='Delay between updates')
    parser.add_argument('-a', '--nsdelay', type=int, default=0, help='Additional nanosecond delay')
    parser.add_argument('-T', '--tty', type=str, help='Display on specific tty')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.version:
        print("TTY-Clock 2 © devel version")
        return
    
    if args.info:
        print("TTY-Clock 2 © by Martin Duquesnoy (xorg62@gmail.com), Grey (grey@greytheory.net)")
        return
    
    if args.help:
        print("usage : tty-clock [-iuvsScbtrahDBxn] [-C [0-7]] [-f format] [-d delay] [-a nsdelay] [-T tty]")
        print("    -s            Show seconds")
        print("    -S            Screensaver mode")
        print("    -x            Show box")
        print("    -c            Set the clock at the center of the terminal")
        print("    -C [0-7]      Set the clock color")
        print("    -b            Use bold colors")
        print("    -t            Set the hour in 12h format")
        print("    -u            Use UTC time")
        print("    -T tty        Display the clock on the specified terminal")
        print("    -r            Do rebound the clock")
        print("    -f format     Set the date format")
        print("    -n            Don't quit on keypress")
        print("    -v            Show tty-clock version")
        print("    -i            Show some info about tty-clock")
        print("    -h            Show this page")
        print("    -D            Hide date")
        print("    -B            Enable blinking colon")
        print("    -d delay      Set the delay between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.")
        print("    -a nsdelay    Additional delay between two redraws in nanoseconds. Default 0ns.")
        return
    
    clock = TTYClock()
    clock.show_seconds = args.seconds
    clock.show_box = args.box
    clock.centered = args.center
    if args.color is not None:
        clock.color = args.color
    clock.bold = args.bold
    clock.h12 = args.12hour
    clock.use_utc = args.utc
    clock.rebound = args.rebound
    if args.format:
        clock.date_format = args.format
    clock.no_exit = args.no_exit
    clock.hide_date = args.hide_date
    clock.blink_colon = args.blink
    clock.delay = args.delay
    clock.delay_ns = args.nsdelay
    clock.screensaver = args.screensaver
    
    try:
        curses.wrapper(clock.run)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

    7: [1,1,0,1,0,0,0],
    8: [1,1,1,1,1,1,1],
    9: [1,1,1,1,1,0,1],
}

            lines[1].append(" ")  # Line 1: empty
            lines[2].append("  ")  # Line 2: middle dots
            lines[3].append(" ")  # Line 3: empty
            lines[4].append(" ")  # Line 4: bottom
        else:
            a,b,g,c,d,e,f = segs
            
            # Line 0: top horizontal (segment a)
            if a:
                lines[0].append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
            else:
                lines[0].append("      ")
            
            # Line 1: top verticals (f=left, b=right)
            left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if f else "  "

            else:
                lines[2].append("      ")
            
            # Line 3: bottom verticals (e=left, c=right)
            left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if e else "  "
            right = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if c else "  "
            lines[3].append(f"{left}  {right}")
            
            # Line 4: bottom horizontal (segment d)
            if d:
                lines[4].append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
            else:
                lines[4].append("      ")
        
        # Add separator between digits
        if idx < len(digit_segments) - 1:
            for i in range(5):
                lines[i].append(" ")
    
    # Format result with leading space
    result = []
    for line in lines:
        result.append(" " + "".join(line))
    
    return result

import sys

    1: [0,1,0,1,0,0,0],
    2: [1,1,1,0,1,1,0],
    3: [1,1,1,1,1,0,0],

    6: [1,0,1,1,1,1,1],
    7: [1,1,0,1,0,0,0],
    8: [1,1,1,1,1,1,1],
    9: [1,1,1,1,1,0,1],
}

# ANSI color codes
color_bg_map = {
    0: "40",  # black
    1: "41",  # red
    2: "42",  # green
    3: "43",  # yellow
    4: "44",  # blue
    5: "45",  # magenta
    6: "46",  # cyan
    7: "47",  # white
}

color_fg_map = {
    1: "31m",  # red
    2: "32m",  # green
}

class TTYClock:
    def __init__(self):
        self.show_seconds = False
        self.show_box = False
        self.centered = False
        self.color = 2
        self.bold = False
        self.use_utc = False
        self.h12 = False
        self.hide_date = False
        self.blink_colon = False
        self.no_exit = False
        self.date_format = "%Y-%m-%d"
        self.delay = 1.0
        self.delay_ns = 0
        self.screensaver = False
        self.running = True
        
    def render_7seg_digit(self, digit, color_on, color_off):
        """Render a single 7-segment digit with colored background"""
        if digit not in segments_map:
            return ["      ", "      ", "      ", "      ", "      "]
        
        segs = segments_map[digit]
        a,b,g,c,d,e,f = segs
        
        lines = []
        
        # Line 0: top horizontal
        if a:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        # Line 1: upper verticals
        left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if f else "  "
        right = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if b else "  "
        lines.append(f"{left}  {right}")
        
        # Line 2: middle horizontal
        if g:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        # Line 3: lower verticals
        left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if e else "  "
        right = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if c else "  "
        lines.append(f"{left}  {right}")
        
        # Line 4: bottom horizontal
        if d:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        return lines
    
    def render_colon(self):
        """Render a colon separator - 6 spaces with no color"""
        return ["      ", "      ", "      ", "      ", "      "]
    
    def render_time_lines(self, time_str, color_on, color_off):
        """Render time as 5 lines"""
        lines = ["", "", "", "", ""]
        
        for char_idx, char in enumerate(time_str):
            if char_idx > 0:
                lines[0] += " "
                lines[1] += " "
                lines[2] += " "
                lines[3] += " "
                lines[4] += " "
            
            if char == ':':
                digit_lines = self.render_colon()
            else:
                digit_lines = self.render_7seg_digit(int(char), color_on, color_off)
            
            for i in range(5):
                lines[i] += digit_lines[i]
        
        return lines
    
    def draw_clock_frame(self):
        """Draw one frame of the clock"""
        # Get current time
        if self.use_utc:
            t = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        else:
            t = datetime.now()
        
        hour = t.hour
        minute = t.minute
        second = t.second
        
        if self.h12:
            if hour > 12:
                hour -= 12
            elif hour == 0:
                hour = 12
        
        # Build time string
        if self.show_seconds:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d}"
        else:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}"
        
        # Color codes
        bg_code = color_bg_map.get(self.color, "42")
        color_on = f"\x1b[{bg_code}m"
        color_off = "\x1b[49m"
        
        if self.bold:
            color_on = "\x1b[1m" + color_on
        
        # Render time
        time_lines = self.render_time_lines(time_str, color_on, color_off)
        
        # Clear screen
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
        
        # Draw time
        for i, line in enumerate(time_lines):
            sys.stdout.write(f" {line}\n")
        
        # Draw date if not hidden
        if not self.hide_date:
            date_str = t.strftime(self.date_format)
            fg_code = color_fg_map.get(1, "32m")
            sys.stdout.write(f"\n            \x1b[{fg_code}{date_str}\x1b[0m\n")
        
        sys.stdout.flush()
    
    def run(self):
        """Main run loop"""
        def signal_handler(sig, frame):
            self.running = False
        
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
        
        # Hide cursor
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        
        try:
            while self.running:
                self.draw_clock_frame()
                
                # Sleep
                sleep_time = self.delay + self.delay_ns / 1e9
                time.sleep(sleep_time)
        finally:
            # Show cursor
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h")
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[0m")  # Reset
            sys.stdout.flush()

    parser.add_argument('-S', '--screensaver', action='store_true')

    parser.add_argument('-f', '--format', type=str)
    parser.add_argument('-n', '--no-exit', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-v', '--version', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-i', '--info', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-D', '--hide-date', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-B', '--blink', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('-d', '--delay', type=float, default=1.0)
    parser.add_argument('-a', '--nsdelay', type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument('-T', '--tty', type=str)
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.version:
        print("TTY-Clock 2 © devel version")
        return
    
    if args.info:
        print("TTY-Clock 2 © by Martin Duquesnoy (xorg62@gmail.com), Grey (grey@greytheory.net)")
        return
    
    if args.help:
        print("usage : tty-clock [-iuvsScbtrahDBxn] [-C [0-7]] [-f format] [-d delay] [-a nsdelay] [-T tty]")
        print("    -s            Show seconds")
        print("    -S            Screensaver mode")
        print("    -x            Show box")
        print("    -c            Set the clock at the center of the terminal")
        print("    -C [0-7]      Set the clock color")
        print("    -b            Use bold colors")
        print("    -t            Set the hour in 12h format")
        print("    -u            Use UTC time")
        print("    -T tty        Display the clock on the specified terminal")
        print("    -r            Do rebound the clock")
        print("    -f format     Set the date format")
        print("    -n            Don't quit on keypress")
        print("    -v            Show tty-clock version")
        print("    -i            Show some info about tty-clock")
        print("    -h            Show this page")
        print("    -D            Hide date")
        print("    -B            Enable blinking colon")
        print("    -d delay      Set the delay between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.")
        print("    -a nsdelay    Additional delay between two redraws in nanoseconds. Default 0ns.")
        return
    
    clock = TTYClock()
    clock.show_seconds = args.seconds
    clock.show_box = args.box
    clock.centered = args.center
    if args.color is not None:
        clock.color = args.color
    clock.bold = args.bold
    clock.h12 = args.format_12hour
    clock.use_utc = args.utc
    clock.rebound = args.rebound
    if args.format:
        clock.date_format = args.format
    clock.no_exit = args.no_exit
    clock.hide_date = args.hide_date
    clock.blink_colon = args.blink
    clock.delay = args.delay
    clock.delay_ns = args.nsdelay
    clock.screensaver = args.screensaver
    
    try:
        clock.run()

}

    0: "40",  # black
    1: "41",  # red
    2: "42",  # green
    3: "43",  # yellow
    4: "44",  # blue
    5: "45",  # magenta
    6: "46",  # cyan
    7: "47",  # white
}

class TTYClock:
    def __init__(self):
        self.show_seconds = False
        self.show_box = False
        self.centered = False
        self.color = 2
        self.bold = False
        self.use_utc = False
        self.h12 = False
        self.hide_date = False
        self.blink_colon = False
        self.no_exit = False
        self.date_format = "%Y-%m-%d"
        self.delay = 1.0
        self.delay_ns = 0
        self.screensaver = False
        self.running = True
        
    def render_7seg_digit(self, digit, color_on, color_off):
        """Render a single 7-segment digit with colored background"""
        if digit not in segments_map:
            return ["      ", "      ", "      ", "      ", "      "]
        
        segs = segments_map[digit]
        a,b,g,c,d,e,f = segs
        
        lines = []
        
        # Line 0: top horizontal
        if a:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        # Line 1: upper verticals
        left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if f else "  "
        right = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if b else "  "
        lines.append(f"{left}  {right}")
        
        # Line 2: middle horizontal
        if g:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        # Line 3: lower verticals
        left = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if e else "  "
        right = f"{color_on}  {color_off}" if c else "  "
        lines.append(f"{left}  {right}")
        
        # Line 4: bottom horizontal
        if d:
            lines.append(f"{color_on}      {color_off}")
        else:
            lines.append("      ")
        
        return lines
    
    def render_colon(self):
        """Render a colon separator - 6 spaces with no color"""
        return ["      ", "      ", "      ", "      ", "      "]
    
    def render_time_lines(self, time_str, color_on, color_off):
        """Render time as 5 lines"""
        lines = ["", "", "", "", ""]
        
        for char_idx, char in enumerate(time_str):
            if char_idx > 0:
                lines[0] += " "
                lines[1] += " "
                lines[2] += " "
                lines[3] += " "
                lines[4] += " "
            
            if char == ':':
                digit_lines = self.render_colon()
            else:
                digit_lines = self.render_7seg_digit(int(char), color_on, color_off)
            
            for i in range(5):
                lines[i] += digit_lines[i]
        
        return lines
    
    def draw_clock_frame(self):
        """Draw one frame of the clock"""
        # Get current time
        if self.use_utc:
            t = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        else:
            t = datetime.now()
        
        hour = t.hour
        minute = t.minute
        second = t.second
        
        if self.h12:
            if hour > 12:
                hour -= 12
            elif hour == 0:
                hour = 12
        
        # Build time string
        if self.show_seconds:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d}"
        else:
            time_str = f"{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}"
        
        # Color codes
        bg_code = color_bg_map.get(self.color, "42")
        color_on = f"\x1b[{bg_code}m"
        color_off = "\x1b[49m"
        
        if self.bold:
            color_on = "\x1b[1m" + color_on
        
        # Render time
        time_lines = self.render_time_lines(time_str, color_on, color_off)
        
        # Clear screen
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
        
        # Draw box if needed
        if self.show_box:
            box_width = 52
            box_height = 6
            
            # Top line
            sys.stdout.write(f" {color_on}l")
            for i in range(box_width - 2):
                sys.stdout.write("q")
            sys.stdout.write(f"k{color_off}\n")
            
            # Draw time lines inside box
            for i, line in enumerate(time_lines):
                if i < box_height - 2:
                    sys.stdout.write(f" {color_on}x{color_off} {line}\n")
            
            # Bottom line
            sys.stdout.write(f" {color_on}m")
            for i in range(box_width - 2):
                sys.stdout.write("q")
            sys.stdout.write(f"j{color_off}\n")
        else:
            # Draw time without box
            for i, line in enumerate(time_lines):
                sys.stdout.write(f" {line}\n")
        
        # Draw date if not hidden
        if not self.hide_date:
            date_str = t.strftime(self.date_format)
            sys.stdout.write(f"\n            \x1b[31m{date_str}\x1b[0m\n")
        
        sys.stdout.flush()
    
    def run(self):
        """Main run loop"""
        def signal_handler(sig, frame):
            self.running = False
        
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
        
        # Hide cursor
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        
        try:
            while self.running:
                self.draw_clock_frame()
                
                # Sleep
                sleep_time = self.delay + self.delay_ns / 1e9
                time.sleep(sleep_time)
        finally:
            # Show cursor
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h")
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[0m")  # Reset
            sys.stdout.flush()

    parser.add_argument('-d', '--delay', type=float, default=1.0)
    parser.add_argument('-a', '--nsdelay', type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument('-T', '--tty', type=str)
    
    args = parser.parse_args()

        print("    -s            Show seconds")

        print("    -C [0-7]      Set the clock color")

        print("    -u            Use UTC time")
        print("    -T tty        Display the clock on the specified terminal")
        print("    -r            Do rebound the clock")
        print("    -f format     Set the date format")
        print("    -n            Don't quit on keypress")
        print("    -v            Show tty-clock version")
        print("    -i            Show some info about tty-clock")
        print("    -h            Show this page")
        print("    -D            Hide date")
        print("    -B            Enable blinking colon")
        print("    -d delay      Set the delay between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.")
        print("    -a nsdelay    Additional delay between two redraws in nanoseconds. Default 0ns.")
        return
    
    clock = TTYClock()
    clock.show_seconds = args.seconds
    clock.show_box = args.box
